name: Radclyffe Hall
bio: Novelist and poet, born Marguerite Antonia Radclyffe-Hall on 12 August 1880, best known for The Well of Loneliness (1928), a serious treatment of lesbianism that was prosecuted and banned in England until 1949. The Ransom Center's biographical sketch records that, "[s]elf-identifying as a sexual 'invert,' Hall adopted a masculine appearance and the name John". Her two long partnerships were with the singer Mabel Batten (1856-1916), her first lover, and with Batten's cousin Una Troubridge (1887-1963), from 1915 until Hall's death. Hall belongs to a later generation than Wilde's circle and does not appear anywhere in his Complete Letters; she reaches this map from the Ives side, as a figure of the homophile politics Ives helped begin. Matt Cook records that she and Troubridge "seem to have been considered" for the Order of Chaeronea and that Ives took an interest in the 1928 obscenity case over her novel. She died on 7 October 1943.
bio_note: The Order-of-Chaeronea and obscenity-case detail from Matt Cook, Queer Domesticities (2014), p. 108; Cook's double hedge is preserved and no Order-membership or Ives edge is created on it.
